identity: WSE is a Python/MCP experiment framework. Its documented November 12 example runs Qwen3-0.6B locally with a remote Codex-driven updater and 16 development and 16 held-out problems. OpenWSP's Experiment 8 targets Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B revision 2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17; its reference and independent live run use different editors/configurations. WeightSpec's RFC-0001 defines a draft patch format. Pin the exact library and artifact revisions in any interop test.
information_and_action_parity: WSE selects candidates on common development questions and seals the test. Its Codex controller can execute shell computation outside metered WSE calls. OpenWSP gives an editor a persistent numerical kernel and bounded forward service. WeightSpec exposes validated JSON operations and metered probes through MCP. Using each project's full editor as an experimental arm would vary allowed operations, compute and evidence simultaneously. For IWIBench, keep all arms in the same native worker and expose identical numerical write expressions.
observation_provenance: OpenWSP records a pinned target, practice files, generation settings and teacher-forced internal observations separately. WSE reports development contrasts in its recorded agent hypotheses. WeightSpec resolves human-readable selectors against concrete architectures. Proposal: log the resolved parameter, exact site and tokenizer positions even if the editor sends only a short ID. Record hash, original revision and public example IDs for every derived operand.
diagnostic_effect: WSE's Qwen3-0.6B example documents residual contrasts used to choose late MLP projections. Selected development accuracy improved 5/16 to 7/16, but held-out accuracy was still 4/16 and cutoffs remained 11/16. This small example is evidence for holding out evaluation, not an estimate of the value of interpretability. WeightSpec documents dose sweeps, direction reversal and matched random-direction controls. [uncertain] Neither establishes that identical IWI actions selected with causal evidence on Gemma improve native held-out reward.
edit_and_replay: WSE documents exact patch replay and candidate freezing before test. OpenWSP verifies the hashes of a released edited checkpoint before evaluating an independently discovered patch. Its archived weight-swap diagnostic says its tested engine lacked the required reload interface. WeightSpec separates JSON recipes and optional safetensors payloads, stores tensor hashes and counts changes after casting to storage dtype. First interop test: convert a known native patch, verify tied rows and final dtype, reapply to a pristine target, check touched and untouched tensor bytes, and independently compare logits and greedy outputs.
patch_quality: OpenWSP reports the released Qwen checkpoint scored 50.6% locally versus its own live rediscovery at 12.9% on MATH-500. Local checkpoint calibration used one generation per problem, live evaluation used four; the latter was one editor search. The contrast illustrates why exact replay and finding a new patch must be tested separately. Absolute Qwen math scores cannot be used as Gemma IWIBench baselines.
updater_cost: [uncertain] No matched IWIBench provider-token comparison for these three frameworks was verified. WSE notes unmetered controller shell execution. OpenWSP distinguishes subscription usage and compute. Log full per-turn requests, cached input, output and actual charged units alongside tool payloads. Compare control and treatment under one tokenizer and context policy.
target_cost: OpenWSP's published trial had a budget of 50 forward passes and 300 Python runs. WeightSpec's successful probe calls decrement a request budget. WSE's max evaluations counts whole-model development evaluations, including the original. These units represent different workloads. [uncertain] Realized Gemma probe cost under the proposed experiment is unmeasured. Normalize comparisons by sequences and tokens, then report wall time, GPU-hours, SAE overhead and final private verifier cost.
uncertainty: The WSE example is small and OpenWSP's live result is one discovery run. Product readmes describe features, not independent proof of parity with the pinned IWI verifier. [uncertain] No IWIBench-to-WeightSpec or OpenWSP round-trip was tested for this research. Validate one numeric alias repair and one low-rank case before exposing optional interoperability.
portability_and_terms: WSE is Apache-2.0, OpenWSP MIT, and WeightSpec Apache-2.0. Confirm terms of any model or patch separately. Documented WSE agent runtime currently requires macOS and Codex CLI; its model and artifact APIs merit separate consideration. OpenWSP exposes one core through CLI/SDK/MCP. WeightSpec's JSON policy plus optional binary payload can be a portable export target. The native IWIBench format remains sufficient for the first study.
sequential_transfer: The cited public experiments build and evaluate one selected patch. For future multi-job tests, carry only cumulative numeric changes plus the pinned immutable target into a cold evaluation process, start each job with fresh prompts and tool state, and measure acquisition, old-task regressions and cumulative cost. Record whether long-term state resides in weights, adapters, stored recipes or external retrieval.
